verdict.root_cause: checkout is crash-looping on an unrecovered nil-pointer dereference in its own PlaceOrder handler (send-to-post-processor path, main.go:630), repeating with an identical fault signature across the window [tr_e2eb7807b28d]. Each crash takes checkout's listener down, which is what frontend's server-side gRPC calls see as status 14 UNAVAILABLE with connection refused / connection dropped against a single upstream IP on port 5050 — checkout's port — with name resolution fine and failures at TCP accept, not at deadline [tr_3382f79d68aa]. The resulting partial failures surface as ~15s client-timeout cut-offs at frontend-proxy and load-generator rather than as elevated frontend error ratios [tr_90a6a61fbe13][tr_4b7fb366dc99][tr_03e3dd383648]. No change of any kind is recorded for checkout [tr_f419323593fd], and frontend's only changes are an unrelated automated CART_ADDR set/revert flap that was already reverted 2.6h before onset [tr_daf4e6c3ed89], so the faulting artifact is a build whose code path dies on live traffic.
verdict.reasoning: Only one service shows a self-originated fatal defect: checkout, with three identical SIGSEGV panics inside its own handler, ruled out as downstream propagation, OOM-kill or graceful shutdown [tr_e2eb7807b28d]. That mechanism predicts exactly what frontend reports — immediate connection-refused/dropped UNAVAILABLE against one upstream address on 5050, not DNS, not TLS, not deadline exhaustion, not a fleet-wide outage [tr_3382f79d68aa]. Frontend and frontend-proxy error ratios are below baseline with only a terminal spike at 05:08:16, so neither is the origin; they are the places the damage was noticed [tr_4b7fb366dc99][tr_03e3dd383648]. Traces show the proxy and cart/product-reviews paths healthy and the failures pinned at a fixed ~15s timeout boundary, the expected caller-side view of an upstream that keeps dying mid-flight [tr_90a6a61fbe13]. I class it bad_deploy because the running checkout build cannot serve its own PlaceOrder path; the rollback claim is the weak link, since no deploy record exists for checkout at all [tr_f419323593fd].
open_questions: No change record covers checkout before onset — the queried window starts at the incident timestamp, so whether a deploy introduced the nil deref is unestablished and the rollback target is unidentified [tr_f419323593fd].
Both log queries are truncated at ~04:52:41; nothing observed speaks to checkout's or frontend's state at 05:07:16 itself [tr_e2eb7807b28d][tr_3382f79d68aa].

The ~15s traces show frontend spans with 100% self-time and no child spans — if checkout were refusing connections, a failed child span would normally appear; the stall is unexplained inside frontend [tr_90a6a61fbe13].
The upstream IP on port 5050 was never resolved to a named service, so the identification of checkout as that peer is inference, not measurement.
No evidence placed checkout's restart/crash timing against the 05:07:16 onset.

alternatives.root_cause: frontend's server process is wedged on the affected request paths — callers hang to a fixed 15s deadline, frontend emits no log lines for the final 16 minutes, and the errored handler spans have no children at all.
alternatives.why_not: Frontend still served a page render and API routes normally in the same window and still produced span data, and its own logs name a concrete refused upstream; a freeze does not explain checkout's panics, whereas checkout's panics do explain frontend's errors.

alternatives.root_cause: An unidentified dependency behind frontend became slow, and frontend failed because it waited out a 15s timeout.
alternatives.why_not: The errored frontend spans have no child spans to attribute a wait to, and the observed failures are connect-time refusals rather than DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; every measured dependency (cart, product-reviews, Redis) completed in milliseconds.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no observable effect is predicted. The mechanism named by the verdict — a nil-pointer panic in checkout's own PlaceOrder handler — lives in a service that is not in this incident's blast radius, so no permitted action can be aimed at it. The three legal targets (frontend-proxy, load-generator, frontend) are all downstream symptom-carriers: frontend's error ratio is *below* baseline at 0.44x [tr_4b7fb366dc99] and frontend's own logs show only transport-level status 14 from an upstream, with frontend itself explicitly ruled out as the faulting component [tr_3382f79d68aa]. Recreating or rolling back any of them would not remove a panic running in another process.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention would be shown wrong by evidence that does not exist in this brief: (a) a change-history query on checkout over a window that actually *starts before* 05:07:16 — the queried window begins at the incident timestamp and returned empty, so it carries no information about a pre-onset deploy [tr_f419323593fd] — naming a prior image tag and a deploy inside the window, which would make rollback_image's preconditions met; (b) resolution of the port-5050 upstream IP to a named service, since the identification of that peer as checkout is inference rather than measurement [tr_3382f79d68aa]; or (c) log or trace coverage at 05:07:16 itself, which both log queries lack — they truncate at ~04:52:41 [tr_e2eb7807b28d][tr_3382f79d68aa]. Separately, the ~15s frontend stalls show 100% self-time with no child spans at all [tr_90a6a61fbe13]; if checkout were refusing connections a failed child span should appear, so a second, unexplained mechanism inside frontend may be in play. If that mechanism were characterised and shown to be process state rather than a change, restart_service on frontend would become arguable — nothing here establishes that yet.
proposal.risk: The risk being avoided is acting on a low-confidence diagnosis whose target is unidentified. rollback_image on frontend would recreate a service that measurement shows is erroring *less* than baseline, discard a working build, and move frontend to an older image on the strength of a change record that contains only CART_ADDR environment flaps and no deploys at all [tr_daf4e6c3ed89] — i.e. there is no prior image tag to roll back to, so the action would either fail or revert something unrelated. restart_service on frontend would clear the ~15s stalls only if they are in-process state; if they are in fact a downstream crash-loop, the restart buys a few minutes of churn, destroys the stalled-request evidence needed to localise the real fault, and the panics resume on the next PlaceOrder. revert_config on frontend would restore the CART_ADDR override that was already reverted 2.6h before onset and was explicitly ruled out as the trigger [tr_daf4e6c3ed89] — actively reintroducing a known-bad pointer to cart:7071. The cost of abstaining is continued partial checkout failure; the cost of each available action is a working service degraded for no mechanistic reason.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody — no change is made, so no caller sees a reset and the incident continues in its current state (intermittent ~15s client-timeout cut-offs at frontend-proxy and load-generator [tr_90a6a61fbe13][tr_03e3dd383648]). For contrast, had an action been taken: any of the three permitted actions recreates one container, and its inbound callers see connection resets for the duration — frontend's recreate would be visible to frontend-proxy and through it to load-generator, i.e. every user-facing path in this incident, including the browse, cart and recommendations routes that are currently succeeding in tens of milliseconds [tr_90a6a61fbe13]. That is the whole alerted surface, which is why it should not be spent on an unestablished target. Escalate to a human with the three open questions above, and in particular re-run change_history on checkout with a window starting several hours before onset; until the port-5050 peer is resolved and a prior image tag exists, the correct remediation lies outside what this system may do.

triage_judgement.reasoning: The edge-facing proxy alerted alongside the load generator, which means user-facing traffic is affected rather than a lone synthetic probe. With no open incident to attribute it to and frontend implicated one hop in, this is not dismissible.
